# external.event_types

## Purpose
Tiny reference/dimension table that maps a numeric `event_type_id` to its raw string code
(`event_type_raw`) and a human-readable `name`. It enumerates the six VAST video-playback
events MNTN fires for a CTV ad: the initial impression, playback start, and the three
quartile checkpoints, ending at complete. Reach for it when you need to decode an
`event_type_id` seen in an impression/event source, or to get a display label — the ordered
ladder is impression(1) → start(2) → 25%(3) → 50%(4) → 75%(5) → complete(6).

Backed by GCS parquet at `gs://mntn-analytics-curated/coredw/public/event_types/*.parquet`
(i.e. the `coredw.public.event_types` dimension exposed as a BigQuery EXTERNAL federated table).

## Grain & keys
- **Grain:** one row per VAST event type. The full table is exactly 6 rows (verified: `COUNT(*)=6`).
- **Key(s) / join columns:** `event_type_id` is the primary key. Empirically all three columns
  are 1:1 and fully distinct across the 6 rows (`COUNT(DISTINCT event_type_id) = COUNT(DISTINCT event_type_raw) = COUNT(DISTINCT name) = 6`),
  so you can join on either `event_type_id` (numeric FK) or `event_type_raw` (string code).

## Column meanings (only the non-obvious ones)
Full contents (all 6 rows, verified live 2026-07-19):

| event_type_id | event_type_raw | name |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | vast_impression | VAST Impression |
| 2 | vast_start | VAST Start |
| 3 | vast_firstQuartile | VAST First Quartile |
| 4 | vast_midpoint | VAST Midpoint |
| 5 | vast_thirdQuartile | VAST Third Quartile |
| 6 | vast_complete | VAST Complete |

- **event_type_id** — numeric FK / primary key (1–6). The ids are ordered along the playback
  lifecycle: impression fires first, then start, then the three quartiles (first=25%,
  midpoint=50%, third=75%), then complete=100%. Nullable in the schema but no NULLs exist.
- **event_type_raw** — the raw string code used as the filter value in the event/impression
  log tables (e.g. `event_type_raw = 'vast_impression'` for the IP-trace lens). Note the mixed
  casing on quartile names (`vast_firstQuartile`, `vast_thirdQuartile`) — copy exactly.
- **name** — display label only ("VAST Impression", "VAST Midpoint", …); no analytical logic
  depends on it.

## Joins & relationships
This is the "1" side of every join — a 6-row lookup, so joining INTO it never fans out.

- **`silver.logdata.event_log`** (VAST event stream, billions of rows) — N:1 into this table on
  `event_log.event_type_id = event_types.event_type_id`. Safe enrichment, no fan-out. Note
  `event_log` already carries `event_type_raw` denormalized, so most queries filter
  `event_log.event_type_raw = 'vast_impression'` directly and never need this lookup at all;
  reach for `event_types` mainly to resolve an id→name or to enumerate the valid codes.
- **`external.vastimpression__v1` / `external.impression__v1`** (CTV-VAST / display impression
  GCS sources) — same N:1 id→code/name resolution if they surface an `event_type_id`.
- Because `event_type_id` and `event_type_raw` are both unique here, either can be the join key;
  prefer `event_type_id` (integer) for join efficiency.

Related VAST-IP gotchas live in the `silver.logdata.event_log` prose section of
`knowledge/data_catalog.md` (TI-650): multiple event types share one `ad_served_id`, so dedup
with `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ad_served_id ORDER BY time)` and take rn=1; all six event
types for a playback share the same IP.

## Gotchas
- **Static content, but not immutable** — the six VAST rows have been stable, but this is a
  federated view of an upstream `coredw.public.event_types` dim; a schema/row change there
  appears here with no BQ-side versioning. Re-dump before assuming ids beyond 6.
- **No time / partition / TTL columns** — pure static dimension; there is no date column to
  filter and nothing ages out.
- **Only VAST events** — this table does NOT enumerate clicks, conversions, or display
  impressions. Display/mobile ads fire no VAST event, so they never appear here or in `event_log`.
- **Casing** — `vast_firstQuartile` / `vast_thirdQuartile` are camel-cased; exact-match filters
  fail silently on a lowercased copy.

## Cost & partitioning notes
- **No partition to filter** — external GCS parquet, `requirePartitionFilter=false`, 6 rows.
  There is no partition column and no meaningful pruning; a `SELECT *` reads the whole object.
- **Cost is negligible.** `bq show` reports `numBytes=0` / `numRows=0` (expected for a federated
  external table — that 0 is not real storage, so `approx_logical_bytes` is left null).
  `bq query --dry_run` on both `SELECT *` and `SELECT event_type_id` reports "lower bound of 0
  bytes" (BigQuery cannot statically size an external parquet source; both columns sets estimate
  identically). At 6 rows the actual scan is trivially cheap regardless of columns selected.
- **External re-reads the GCS object each run** — no partition/BQ-storage caching the way a
  native table has. It's tiny, so this doesn't matter, but in a big join let the optimizer
  broadcast it (it's the small side) rather than materializing it repeatedly.

## Example queries
```sql
-- Enumerate the VAST ladder
SELECT event_type_id, event_type_raw, name
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.event_types`
ORDER BY event_type_id;

-- Resolve ids to human names when enriching an impression/event source
SELECT e.*, t.name AS event_name
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.vastimpression__v1` e
LEFT JOIN `dw-main-bronze.external.event_types` t
  USING (event_type_id);
```
